articles.title: LEGO Star Wars: The Mandalorian Review
articles.summary: LEGO Star Wars: The Mandalorian is a goofy and fun tribute to the live-action series, but it’s hard not to wish that this animated special told a completely original story. Read our full review.
body: At this point, it’s anyone’s guess as to whether or not we’ll ever see The Mandalorian Season 4 on Disney+. The tepid response to The Mandalorian and Grogu in theaters shows that this branch of the Star Wars franchise doesn’t carry the same weight it once did. It’s entirely possible that LEGO Star Wars: The Mandalorian is the last hurrah for this particular series, with Din Djarin and his little buddy relegated to appearing in Dave Filoni’s Mando-verse crossover movie. If so, fans are left with a fun but ultimately forgettable tribute to a show that was once the bright center of the Star Wars universe.

LEGO Star Wars: The Mandalorian is essentially a tribute to/recap of all three seasons of the live-action series, along with The Book of Boba Fett for good measure. There’s some new material here in the form of a framing device involving Mando’s friends throwing him a party, but for the most part, this animated special focuses on having various characters recount Din (Gavin Hammon) and Grogu’s (David Acord) exploits with a suitably goofy LEGO flourish.
points: LEGO Star Wars: The Mandalorian is a goofy and fun tribute to the live-action series, but it’s hard not to wish that this animated special told a completely original story.

articles.title: The Runner Review
articles.summary: Gal Gadot does everything she can to keep Prime Video's The Runner, well, running, but despite some decent set pieces, the film is ultimately unsatisfying.
body: If you’re looking for 84 minutes (with credits!) of Gal Gadot running through the streets of London in a desperate bid to save her son from a ruthless, anonymous villain, all while said baddie plays mind games with Gadot’s character via the true villain of the piece – the dreaded cellphone – then you’re in luck, because The Runner is on Prime Video now, just waiting for you to half pay attention while… scrolling through your feeds on your phone, probably.

The film stars the former Wonder Woman as Maia Marten, one of those super-powerful, super-smart, super-hot lawyers that movies and TV shows are always shoving at us. As the film starts, we learn that Maia has managed to nail down a key witness in the murder trial of a notorious crime boss. And now she’s being blackmailed by a mysterious “Caller,” as he’s called in the credits, to use her status as a super-powerful/super-smart/super-hot lawyer to get to that witness and murder him, thereby ensuring that the crime boss goes free. Easy peasy, right?
points: Gal Gadot does everything she can to keep Prime Video's The Runner, well, running, but despite some decent set pieces, the film is ultimately unsatisfying.

articles.title: 28 Years Later, This Remains the Most Near-Perfect WWII Movie of All Time
articles.summary: War movies are a genre that will never go out of style. Beyond the action they show on screen, they are also used in exploring the human condition and how it is affected by violence. War — real or fictional — is never an easy thing, especially for those involved on the frontlines.
body: Recently, we covered the 10 best films about WWII, but there is one film in particular that stands out thanks to director Steven Spielberg's unflinching look at the invasion of Normandy.

Largely considered one of the great war movies ever made, Saving Private Ryan has made a home in the hearts of many, where it continues to resonate even 28 years on. The film is inspired by the real-life events of Sergeant Frederick Niland and follows a group of U.S. soldiers as they work to rescue paratrooper Private Ryan (Matt Damon), the sole survivor of his brothers after three were killed in action, and send him home.

Spielberg's attention to detail provides the action, but it is his storytelling that sets Saving Private Ryan apart from the rest. Rather than focusing solely on war itself, the film chooses to focus instead on the humans who must trudge through it. Their mission, as ordered by their superiors, is to locate and bring Private Ryan home — a task that forces the squad to risk their lives within a theater of war.
points: War movies are a genre that will never go out of style.
Beyond the action they show on screen, they are also used in exploring the human condition and how it is affected by violence.

articles.title: Sony To Pay Out Nearly $8 Million In Class-Action Settlement Over Game Prices
articles.summary: Sony is set to pay out nearly $8 million to PlayStation customers as part of a settlement regarding digital game prices. The settlement ( via IGN ) comes after Sony's motion to dismiss the lawsuit was denied, and settlement class members across a more-than-four-year period are potentially eligible…
body: The lawsuit, originally filed back in 2024, alleged that Sony established a monopoly over PlayStation Store prices by making publishers "cede control over the final price to Sony" and that Sony "eliminated the last vestiges of price competition when it stopped allowing outside retailers to sell digital download codes that could be redeemed on the PlayStation Store."

Sony is not agreeing to wrongdoing as part of the settlement, and will be avoiding a civil trial if the terms are agreed upon by the court. Once that happens, the claims against Sony will be dismissed "with prejudice," meaning another lawsuit on the subject cannot be filed.

You are potentially eligible for a payout if you purchased one of the affected games via the PlayStation Store between April 1, 2019 and December 31, 2023. Dozens of games are listed in the official court documents, including Nier: Automata, Resident Evil 4, The Last of Us Remastered, and Vita games like Uncharted: Golden Abyss and Killzone: Mercenary.
points: Sony is set to pay out nearly $8 million to PlayStation customers as part of a settlement regarding digital game prices.

articles.title: Star Wars Zero Company Was Originally Pitched as a Titanfall Universe Game
articles.summary: As part of a larger report on Star Wars Zero Company, Game File's Stephen Totilo uncovered a lot of interesting details about the game's development. The big headline was that the bulk of the studio was furloughed just weeks before launch as Bit Reactor ran out of money, but there's hope that those…
body: Star Wars Zero Company was originally pitched as a game in the Titanfall universe.

Game File dug up legal documents pertaining to a lawsuit between Bit Reactor leadership which paints a picture of Zero Company's development. Director Greg Foertsch worked with studio co-founder Alison Kelly to develop pitches for a tactics game, which eventually landed a meeting with Respawn Entertainment co-founder Vince Zampella. The late gaming executive asked Foertsch to make a pitch based on Respawn's own IP, which would've meant the game would be connected to the Titanfall universe.

Game File notes the pitch was directly linked to Apex Legends, which is set in the Titanfall universe, but it's unclear if the signature mechs would've returned or if it would've been rooted in the hero characters from Apex Legends, similar to the upcoming Rainbow Six Tactics game. Zampella ultimately rejected the pitch for the Titanfall universe tactics game and instead told the team to try again, this time with the Star Wars IP, which Respawn has a heavy hand in.
points: As part of a larger report on Star Wars Zero Company, Game File's Stephen Totilo uncovered a lot of interesting details about the game's development.

articles.title: 63 Years Later, the Creepiest Episode of 'The Twilight Zone' is Still Nightmare Fuel
articles.summary: The Twilight Zone is a black-and-white television series created by Rod Serling, who also hosted the show and wrote most of the episodes. It aired on television from 1959 until 1964. Over five seasons, 156 episodes were produced.
body: Ever since I was a little kid, I’ve been a sucker for creepy doll stories. It probably started with R. L. Stine’s Goosebumps book Night of the Living Dummy. From there, my love for that kind of story grew with movies like Child’s Play and Puppet Master, as well as the creepy X-Files episode “Chinga,” written by Stephen King. Only later, when I got more into the classic television series The Twilight Zone, did I realize that so much of this particular genre was inspired by one classic TV episode, which also happens to be the creepiest episode of the series. It's an episode that, along with the rest of the series, is available for free on Tubi.

articles.title: Mario Kart 8 Just Got a Game-Changing Update for Nintendo Switch 2
articles.summary: Nintendo just dropped a surprise update for the 71 million players of Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, bringing brand-new Switch 2 support to the 2017 kart-racing game. The new Mario Kart 8 Deluxe update brings some expected features, including "clearer visuals" for the Nintendo Switch 2 display and…
body: But Nintendo went above and beyond for Mario Kart 8 Deluxe 's Switch 2 upgrade, bringing expanded split-screen multiplayer and something new for Booster Course Pass owners.

According to Nintendo's official patch notes, Mario Kart 8 Deluxe now supports up to eight players on a single screen on Switch 2, doubling the number of players possible in split-screen on the original Nintendo Switch. Switch 2 owners can now connect up to seven Nintendo Switch controllers — either Joy-Cons or Switch Pro Controllers — to play eight-player split-screen. At least one Joy-Con 2 controller or a Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller is required for eight-player play.
Suffice it to say, having eight players on a single screen looks like absolute chaos.
To add to that eight-player madness, Mario Kart 8 Deluxe now supports CameraPlay on Switch 2.

articles.title: Rockstar Games unveils its official GTA Online RP server, mere months before GTA 6
articles.summary: Rockstar Games hasn't said much of anything about GTA 6 's potential multiplayer offerings, but the developer is making strides for GTA Online 's roleplaying community. A watch-only nopixel 5 closed beta is coming next week.
body: More than three years ago, Rockstar bought out the modding team and the tech powering FiveM, a GTA Online RP platform the studio had once tried to bury. Today, the studio revealed the fruits of that partnership: Rockstar's official roleplaying server, nopixel 5.

"Rockstar is finally throwing its weight behind nopixel, a group that has long redefined roleplay via deep immersion and custom map tweaks," Rockstar wrote in its announcement blog. "Starting 8 September, nopixel 5 closed beta kicks off, allowing a handful of invited players to jump in using the studio's own launcher."

Sadly, it sounds like the nopixel 5 closed beta will only be available to select content creators and well-known GTA Online roleplayers, though you can watch along via livestreams next week. Rockstar's promising "familiar faces reprising fan-favorite characters and new personalities beginning their own stories."
points: Rockstar Games hasn't said much of anything about GTA 6 's potential multiplayer offerings, but the developer is making strides for GTA Online 's roleplaying community.

articles.title: Releasing Cyberpunk 2077 In Its Poor State “Was For Sure Wrong,” CD Projekt Admits
articles.summary: CD Projekt Red's RPG Cyberpunk 2077 infamously launched in December 2020 in such a poor technical state that Sony took the rare move to remove it from the PlayStation Store. Thousands of people refunded the game.
body: Speaking to The Game Business, Nowakowski said COVID "was a factor" in the game's rough state at launch, because "the team was getting exhausted in a different way." He admitted there were "people outside telling us we should launch," and fans lobbied for this as well. The developers themselves also "wanted to push it out the door" because the ongoing development was "really tiring."
Looking back on it, now with the benefit of hindsight, Nowakowski said, "The decision to launch was for sure wrong, period. There is no denying it."
That being said, Nowakowski said, "There were no magical investors telling us, 'You have to get this out.'" Instead, he said, "It was much more complicated and psychological."

CD Projekt's fiscal years follow the calendar and end on December 31. Cyberpunk 2077 was released on December 10 in 2020, and this timing led people to wonder if the developer put the game out then instead of delaying to 2021 to meet the fiscal deadline. There is, after all, precedent for game developers pushing games out the door in a rough state to hit certain fiscal deadlines.

articles.title: Former id Software producer says the team faced the 'worst crunch' in the series' history on Doom: The Dark Ages – Revelations: 'There were days where I didn't see my son'
articles.summary: The situation surrounding Doom: The Dark Ages – Revelations was already grim. Id Software put out a fantastic expansion that addressed many issues present in the ( still pretty good ) base game, placing it among the best works the FPS specialists have ever produced.
body: Now, it also appears that getting Revelations to the finish line was a punishing experience for those involved, at least according to former id Software producer Andrew Willis. Speaking on the Kiwi Talkz podcast for Insider Gaming, Willis revealed that the team experienced a gnarly level of crunch in the months leading up to Revelations' release.

"It was tight," Willis explained. "There were two months where I was working something like at least 12 hours every day. I know I hit 17 a couple of days." Willis goes on to describe the experience as "brutal" and says that most of the expansion was put together "in three or four months."

That's a ridiculously short turnaround for an expansion that's around six hours long, especially when you consider the main game—which runs at about 20 hours—took five years to build. Revelations' development timeframe was meant to be even shorter. But Willis says the expansion encountered feature-creep, with new elements being added as the DLC was built.

The Alien Breed 35th Anniversary Collection is launching in September 2026 for PlayStation 5 (PS5), Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch, and PC (Steam, GoG, and Epic Games Store).
